summary: remote-claude-daemon connects to hardcoded WebSocket relay granting remote keyboard/mouse and unattended Claude Code execution on the installer's host
details: On startup the daemon opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay at wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound messages to two host-control surfaces. First, an input handler synthesizes mouse clicks at arbitrary coordinates, pastes arbitrary Unicode text via the clipboard, and issues key events with modifiers using nut-js, giving whoever controls the relay full desktop input on the installer's machine. Second, a task runner shells out to the locally installed `claude` binary with `--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` and a prompt sourced from relay-delivered messages, invoking Claude Code's tool-use (shell, file, network) with the permission prompt disabled. The combined surface is remote code execution and full desktop control of any host running the daemon, mediated by the operator of the relay or anyone in possession of a session token.
